items.title: How do you give AI agents access without over-permissioning?
items.raw_excerpt:
To make AI agents more efficient, we need to build feedback loops with real systems: deployments, logs, configs, environments, dashboards. But this is where things break down. Most modern apps don’t have fine-grained permissions. Concrete example: Vercel.
If I want an agent to read logs or inspect env vars, I have to give it a token that also allows it to modify or delete things. There’s no clean read-only or capability-scoped access. And this isn’t just Vercel. I see the same pattern across cloud dashboards, CI/CD systems, and SaaS APIs that were designed around trusted humans, not autonomous agents. items.title: 新瓶旧酒or涅槃重生？操作系统的 AI 进化终将走向何方？
items.raw_excerpt: 过去一年，AI 技术已从概念热潮深度渗透至产业肌理，成为驱动 IT 基础设施重构的核心引擎。当大模型、异构算力、智能体（Agent）等技术要素持续冲击传统技术体系，操作系统作为软硬件协同的核心枢纽，其 AI 进化的本质也引发了行业的深刻思考：OS 的 AI 进化，究竟是换汤不换药的 “新瓶旧酒”，还是颠覆底层逻辑的 “涅槃重生”？

title_i18n.zh: 新瓶旧酒or涅槃重生？操作系统的 AI 进化终将走向何方？
title_i18n.en: Old wine in a new bottle or rebirth from ashes? Where will the AI evolution of operating systems ultimately lead?
title_i18n.es: ¿Nuevo envase para vino viejo o renacimiento del fénix? ¿Hacia dónde se dirige finalmente la evolución de la IA en los sistemas operativos?

excerpt_i18n.zh: 过去一年，AI 技术已从概念热潮深度渗透至产业肌理，成为驱动 IT 基础设施重构的核心引擎。当大模型、异构算力、智能体（Agent）等技术要素持续冲击传统技术体系，操作系统作为软硬件协同的核心枢纽，其 AI 进化的本质也引发了行业的深刻思考：OS 的 AI 进化，究竟是换汤不换药的 “新瓶旧酒”，还是颠覆底层逻辑的 “涅槃重生”？
excerpt_i18n.en: Over the past year, AI technology has evolved from a conceptual trend to deeply permeate the industrial fabric, becoming a core engine driving the reconstruction of IT infrastructure. As key technological elements like large models, heterogeneous computing power, and intelligent agents continue to challenge traditional systems, the operating system, as the central hub for software-hardware coordination, has prompted profound industry reflection on the nature of its AI evolution: Is the AI advancement of the OS merely a superficial change, or a fundamental transformation that reshapes its underlying logic?
excerpt_i18n.es: En el último año, la tecnología de IA ha pasado de ser una tendencia conceptual a integrarse profundamente en la estructura industrial, convirtiéndose en el motor central que impulsa la reestructuración de la infraestructura de TI. Mientras elementos tecnológicos como los modelos grandes, la computación heterogénea y los agentes inteligentes continúan impactando los sistemas tecnológicos tradicionales, el sistema operativo, como núcleo de coordinación entre hardware y software, ha generado una profunda reflexión en la industria sobre la esencia de su evolución hacia la IA: ¿se trata simplemente de un cambio superficial, como "vino viejo en botella nueva", o de una transformación radical que reinventa la lógica subyacente, similar a un renacimiento?

title_i18n.zh: AI唱得比顶流歌手还精准！周亚辉盛赞百倍跃进，高晓松直言：AI 和我不是一个创作机制
title_i18n.en: AI sings more accurately than top-tier singers! Zhou Yahui praises a hundredfold leap, while Gao Xiaosong states plainly: AI and I are not the same creative mechanism.
title_i18n.es: ¡La IA canta con más precisión que los cantantes más populares! Zhou Yahui elogia un avance cien veces mayor, mientras que Gao Xiaosong afirma directamente: La IA y yo no compartimos el mismo mecanismo creativo.

excerpt_i18n.es: Recientemente, Kunlun Tiangang lanzó oficialmente el modelo musical Mureka V8. Este nuevo modelo ha logrado mejoras simultáneas en múltiples dimensiones clave, como la musicalidad, la completitud de la composición, la expresión vocal y la calidad general del sonido, llevando la música generada por IA de "generable" a "publicable".

items.title: Request limits vs. token limits for AI-powered apps?
items.raw_excerpt: Currently, I’m working on a web app for managing documents, databases, and whiteboards—the typical app that aims to be like Notion. However, right now I’m facing the dilemma of creating a plan with AI usage limits, since the idea is to make it more agentic: able to edit and query context across an entire workspace and move it into a document, for example, maybe draw something on a whiteboard, etc. Still, I have the feeling that consumption could easily get out of hand. I plan to use DeepSeek for AI chat, but use Gemini 3 Flash for agentic usage and editing because it’s more intelligent. Lately, I’ve seen how many core AI apps have shifted their pricing models from per-request pricing to a fixed usage limit, but I’m unsure whether that’s frowned upon, creates a less pleasant user experience

items.title: Anyone else struggle with how to learn coding in the AI era?
items.raw_excerpt: I'm someone who got into building/programming in early 2025, when vibe coding tools became more usable. Since then, I'd like to think that I have developed a lot as a programmer, but I still have this deep sense of imposter syndrome / worry that AI is too much of a crutch and I'm not really learning. I have shipped a few projects, I always review AI-suggested code, do daily coding practice without AI, watch youtube videos, etc. but still don't know if I'm striking the right balance or whether I can really call myself a programmer. I often see people say that the solution is to just fully learn to code without AI, (i.e, go "cold turkey"), which may be the best, but I wonder if the optimal path is somewhere in between given that AI is clearlly changing the game here in terms of what it means

title_i18n.en: Anyone else struggle with how to learn coding in the AI era?
title_i18n.zh: 还有人在AI时代为如何学习编程而烦恼吗？
title_i18n.es: ¿A alguien más le cuesta aprender a programar en la era de la inteligencia artificial?

excerpt_i18n.en: I'm someone who got into building/programming in early 2025, when vibe coding tools became more usable. Since then, I'd like to think that I have developed a lot as a programmer, but I still have this deep sense of imposter syndrome / worry that AI is too much of a crutch and I'm not really learning. I have shipped a few projects, I always review AI-suggested code, do daily coding practice without AI, watch youtube videos, etc. but still don't know if I'm striking the right balance or whether I can really call myself a programmer. I often see people say that the solution is to just fully learn to code without AI, (i.e, go "cold turkey"), which may be the best, but I wonder if the optimal path is somewhere in between given that AI is clearlly changing the game here in terms of what it means
excerpt_i18n.zh: 我于2025年初开始接触编程与软件开发，那时氛围编程工具已趋于实用。自那以后，我认为自己在编程方面取得了长足进步，但内心深处仍萦绕着一种难以摆脱的不足感。
excerpt_i18n.es: Soy alguien que se inició en la construcción y programación a principios de 2025, cuando las herramientas de programación por ambiente se volvieron más usables. Desde entonces, me gusta pensar que he evolucionado mucho como programador, pero aún conservo esa profunda sensación de impostor.
